mainTopic: הושע's lesson that הקב"ה never abandons ישראל, followed by teachings on לשון הרע and on the purpose of גלות and the exile to בבל
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's story about the נביא הושע, who had told הקב"ה to replace ישראל with another nation. The גמרא explains the names of his wife גמר בת דבלים and quotes the פסוקים about her three children, whose names are signs of punishment. הקב"ה tells הושע to separate from his wife, as משה did. When הושע says he cannot leave the mother of his children, הקב"ה turns this back on him: how could He abandon ישראל, one of His four acquisitions? הושע prays for ישראל, and the three punishing names become blessings. More teachings follow from פסוקים in הושע: authority shortens its holders' lives, ירבעם was honored for refusing לשון הרע about עמוס, God remembers רחמים even in anger, and גלות brings גרים. The amud then explains why scattering ישראל among the nations was a kindness, and gives several reasons why the exile was to בבל. עולא's reason begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining the name דבלים as bad reputation
steps.stepSummary: The name דבלים is read as דיבה רעה, a bad reputation, doubled: she was a woman of bad reputation, and the daughter of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'דבלים': a woman of bad reputation, daughter of a woman of bad reputation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the name 'דבלים' (גמר's parent, in 'גמר בת דבלים') as a hint to her bad character.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דבלים sounds like דיבה (a bad report). Its doubled ending (-ים) is read as two generations of bad reputation, mother and daughter. This shows the wife was a זונה, exactly as the פסוק describes.

keyTerms.meaning: דבלים, the name of גמר's parent; read here as a wordplay

phrases.english: 'Diblaim':
phrases.notes: End of the quoted פסוק 'גמר בת דבלים' (Hosea 1:3), which began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: ill repute, daughter of ill repute.
phrases.notes: The word is read as doubled, so it points to two generations of bad reputation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְלָיִם דִּבָּה רָעָה בַּת דִּבָּה רָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier explanation of the פסוק 'וילך ויקח את גמר בת דבלים'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דבלים means a woman of ill repute, daughter of a woman of ill repute.

steps.title: שמואל: sweet like a fig cake
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reads דבלים as coming from דבילה, a pressed fig cake: she was 'sweet' to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: she was sweet in everyone's mouth like a fig cake.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל offers a second explanation of the name דבלים, based on the word for a fig cake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of דיבה (bad report), שמואל connects the name to דבילה (fig cake). Like a sweet cake that everyone enjoys, she was desired by everyone. This is a polite way of saying she was a זונה.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
that she was sweet in everyone's mouth like a fig cake.
phrases.notes: A delicate way of describing her immoral behavior.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר שֶׁמְּתוּקָה בְּפִי הַכֹּל כִּדְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the word דבלים than step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דבלים comes from דבילה: she was 'sweet' to all.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: trampled like a fig cake
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also uses the fig cake, but compares her to figs that are trampled and pressed down by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: everyone trampled upon her like a fig cake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third explanation of דבלים, still based on the fig cake but from a different angle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fig cake is made by pressing and stamping the figs down. רבי יוחנן uses 'treading' (דשין) as a polite expression for relations. The point is that everyone had relations with her.

keyTerms.meaning: tread / trample (a polite expression for relations)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
that everyone would tread upon her like a fig cake.
phrases.notes: Pressed figs are stamped down to form a cake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר שֶׁהַכֹּל דָּשִׁין בָּהּ כִּדְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same root as שמואל (דבילה) but with a different image.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דבלים hints that everyone 'trampled' her like pressed figs.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the name גמר means enemies tried to finish ישראל's wealth
steps.stepSummary: Another reading treats the name גמר as a hint about the nation: in her days, enemies wanted to 'finish off' ישראל's money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Gomer.' רבי יהודה said: in her days they sought to finish off the money of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the wife's own name, גמר, as a hint to what happened to ישראל in that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the names described her character. Here the name גמר is read from the root 'to finish.' According to רבי יהודה, the enemies only tried (ביקשו) to wipe out ישראל's wealth.

keyTerms.meaning: גמר, the name of הושע's wife

phrases.english: Alternatively: 'Gomer':
Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבִּקְּשׁוּ לְגַמֵּר מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיָמֶיהָ,
phrases.english: that they sought to finish the money of Israel in her days.
phrases.notes: The key word is 'sought': they wanted to, not necessarily succeeded.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר גּוֹמֶר אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the parent's name (דבלים) to the wife's own name (גמר).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גמר hints that in her time the enemies tried to destroy ישראל's wealth.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: they actually plundered and finished it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן goes further: the enemies did not only try, they really did loot and wipe out ישראל's wealth. He proves this from a פסוק about the king of ארם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: they plundered and finished it, as it says: 'For the king of Aram destroyed them and made them like dust for threshing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי יהודה on how far it went. He says the plundering really happened, and he brings a פסוק to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is 'sought to' (רבי יהודה) versus 'did it' (רבי יוחנן). The פסוק in מלכים ב׳ says ארם made ישראל 'like dust for threshing.' That shows the destruction was carried out completely.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is stated (introduces a proof verse)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
they plundered and finished it,
as it is stated:
'For the king of Aram destroyed them'
phrases.notes: II Kings 13:7

phrases.english: 'and made them like the dust in threshing.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר בָּזְזוּ וְגָמְרוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond רבי יהודה's reading: the destruction actually happened, it was not only attempted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In גמר's days ישראל's wealth was actually plundered and destroyed, as the פסוק about ארם shows.

steps.title: The three children of הושע and their names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוקים in הושע: גמר bears a son named יזרעאל, a daughter named לא רוחמה, and a son named לא עמי. Each name is a message of punishment for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: She conceived and bore him a son. ה׳ said: call him יזרעאל, because soon I will punish the house of יהוא for the blood of יזרעאל and end the kingdom of ישראל. She conceived again and bore a daughter. He said: call her לא רוחמה, because I will no longer have mercy on ישראל. She conceived and bore a son. He said: call him לא עמי, because you are not My people and I will not be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story by quoting the פסוקים about the three children. This sets up the next scene, which takes place after their birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each child's name is a warning: יזרעאל (punishment for bloodshed), לא רוחמה ('no mercy'), and לא עמי ('not My people'). The names show הקב"ה distancing Himself from ישראל. This is the background to what הקב"ה says to הושע next.

keyTerms.meaning: יזרעאל, the first son's name; also the place of יהוא's bloodshed
'not My people', the second son's name
and I will punish / take account

phrases.english: 'And she conceived, and bore him a son.'
phrases.notes: Hosea 1:3

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֵלָיו קְרָא שְׁמוֹ יִזְרְעֶאל
phrases.english: 'And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezreel,'
'for in a little while I will visit'

phrases.aramaic: אֶת דְּמֵי יִזְרְעֶאל עַל בֵּית יֵהוּא
phrases.english: 'the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu,'
'and I will end the kingdom of the house of Israel.'
'And she conceived again and bore a daughter.'

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ קְרָא שְׁמָהּ לֹא רֻחָמָה
phrases.english: 'And He said to him: Call her name Lo-ruhamah,'
'for I will no longer'
'have compassion upon the house of Israel,'
'that I should bear with them.'
'And she conceived and bore a son.'

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר (ה׳ אֵלָיו) קְרָא שְׁמוֹ לֹא עַמִּי
phrases.english: 'And He said: Call his name Lo-ammi,'
'for you are not My people,'
'and I will not be yours.'
phrases.notes: End of the quoted section (Hosea 1:9).

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתַּהַר וַתֵּלֶד לוֹ בֵּן וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֵלָיו קְרָא שְׁמוֹ יִזְרְעֶאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the wife's names, the story moves forward to the birth of her children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three children are born, each given a name that signals punishment and distance from ישראל.

steps.title: God tells הושע to learn from משה and separate from his wife
steps.stepSummary: After the three children are born, הקב"ה challenges הושע. משה separated from his wife once הקב"ה spoke with him, so הושע should do the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: After two sons and one daughter were born to him, הקב"ה said to הושע: Shouldn't you have learned from משה your teacher? Once I spoke with him, he separated from his wife. You too, separate yourself from her.
steps.whatsHappening: הקב"ה confronts הושע with the example of משה רבינו and tells him to separate from his wife. This is a test that sets up the main lesson of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה separated from his wife because a נביא who speaks with הקב"ה often must always be ready. הקב"ה applies this to הושע. In fact, הקב"ה is setting a trap so that הושע's own answer will teach him something.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.confusionAlert: הקב"ה is not really expecting הושע to leave his family. He is setting up הושע to see, from his own reaction, why הקב"ה would never abandon ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ [לוֹ] שְׁנֵי בָנִים וּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: After two sons and one daughter had been born to him,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהוֹשֵׁעַ:
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Hoshea:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה לְךָ לִלְמוֹד מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבָּךְ?
phrases.english: Shouldn't you have learned from Moshe your teacher?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a rebuke.

phrases.english: For once I spoke with him,
he separated from his wife.
You too, separate yourself from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הָיָה לְךָ לִלְמוֹד מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes place after the three children named in step 6 are born.
steps.kashyaTarget: הושע's remaining married to his wife while serving as a נביא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה separated from his wife once הקב"ה spoke with him, so הושע, also a נביא, should do the same.

steps.title: הושע answers that he cannot send away the mother of his children
steps.stepSummary: הושע replies that he has children from this woman, so he cannot send her away or divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to Him: Master of the Universe, I have children from her, and I cannot send her away or divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: הושע pushes back: his family bond is too strong to break. This answer sets up הקב"ה's lesson in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though his wife is a זונה, הושע feels attached to her because they share children. This is exactly the feeling הקב"ה wants him to recognize. ישראל are הקב"ה's children, so He will not exchange them, even when they sin.
steps.whatToRemember: The names דבלים and גמר hint at the wife's bad character and at ישראל's troubles. After three children with warning names are born, הקב"ה tells הושע to separate from his wife like משה did. הושע says he cannot leave the mother of his children. That answer prepares the lesson: הקב"ה will not abandon ישראל, His children.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer is the turning point of the story. הושע had wanted הקב"ה to replace ישראל with another nation, but now he discovers he cannot even abandon his own imperfect family.

phrases.english: He said to Him: Master of the Universe,
I have children from her,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אֲנִי יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיאָהּ וְלֹא לְגָרְשָׁהּ.
phrases.english: and I am unable to send her away or to divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם יֵשׁ לִי בָּנִים מִמֶּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers הקב"ה's demand in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical/emotional objection: the children create a bond that cannot be broken.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הושע should separate from his wife, as משה did.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because they share children, הושע cannot send her away. This prepares הקב"ה's lesson about ישראל.

steps.title: God turns הושע's own answer back on him
steps.stepSummary: הקב"ה points out that הושע will not leave children he is not even sure are his. So how can הקב"ה give up on ישראל, who are truly His children?
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב"ה said to him: You have a wife who is a זונה and children of זנונים. You do not even know if they are yours or someone else's, and still you will not leave them. Then how could I leave ישראל? They are My children, the children of My tested ones, the children of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, and they are one of the four acquisitions I acquired in My world.
steps.whatsHappening: הקב"ה takes הושע's reply from the last step ("I have children, I can't send her away") and uses it to rebuke him. This was the point of the whole marriage from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier הושע had told הקב"ה to replace ישראל with another nation. Now הושע himself has shown that a parent does not abandon his children, even doubtful ones. So the comparison works with extra force: ישראל are certainly הקב"ה's children, so He will surely never abandon them.

keyTerms.meaning: children of My tested ones (the אבות who passed God's tests)
an acquisition, something that belongs specially to its owner

steps.confusionAlert: The command to marry גמר was not a punishment for הושע. It was a lesson set up from the start, so that הושע would feel how a parent cannot give up on children.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main message of the story: הקב"ה's bond with ישראל can never be cancelled, even when they sin.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
Just as you, whose wife is a prostitute,
phrases.notes: וּמָה opens a comparison: if this is true for you, how much more so for Me.

phrases.english: and your children are children of prostitution,
and you do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִם שֶׁלְּךָ הֵן אִם שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים הֵן —
phrases.english: whether they are yours or whether they belong to others,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves this part out, but the point is: either way, you wouldn't leave them.

phrases.english: so too with Israel, who are My sons,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי בְּחוּנַי בְּנֵי אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: the sons of My tested ones, the sons of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob,
one of the four acquisitions that I acquired in My world.
phrases.notes: This line sets up the list in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה אַתָּה שֶׁאִשְׁתְּךָ זוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses הושע's answer in step 8 as the basis for rebuking him.
steps.kashyaTarget: הושע's earlier suggestion that הקב"ה replace ישראל with another nation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a man will not abandon children who may not even be his, then הקב"ה certainly will not abandon ישראל, who are definitely His children.

steps.title: The four acquisitions of God, and the final rebuke
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists the four things הקב"ה acquired, each with a פסוק that uses a form of the word קנה. ישראל is one of them, so how could הושע say to replace them?
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה is one acquisition, as it says: "ה׳ acquired me as the beginning of His way." Heaven and earth are one acquisition, as it says: "Owner of heaven and earth." The בית המקדש is one acquisition, as it says: "This mountain that His right hand acquired." ישראל is one acquisition, as it says: "This nation that You acquired." And you said to exchange them for another nation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim that ישראל is one of הקב"ה's four acquisitions by bringing a פסוק for each one. Then it ends with the sharp rebuke to הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק contains a form of the root קנה (to acquire). That is the proof that each item is a special possession of הקב"ה. Putting ישראל on the same list as the תורה, the world and the בית המקדש shows how unthinkable it is to trade them away.

keyTerms.meaning: acquired me (said by the תורה in משלי)

steps.confusionAlert: "ואתה אמרת העבירם באומה אחרת" refers back to the start of the story on this דף. When הקב"ה told הושע that ישראל had sinned, הושע answered that He should replace them with another nation.

phrases.english: Torah is one acquisition, as it is written:
"The Lord acquired me as the beginning of His way" (Proverbs 8:22).
Heaven and earth are one acquisition, as it is written:
"Owner of heaven and earth" (Genesis 14:19).
The Holy Temple is one acquisition, as it is written:
"This mountain, which His right hand acquired" (Psalms 78:54).
Israel is one acquisition, as it is written:
"The nation that You acquired" (Exodus 15:16).
And you said to replace them with another nation?!
phrases.notes: This is the punch line of the whole rebuke.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרָה קִנְיָן אֶחָד, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim from step 9 that ישראל is one of four acquisitions, then finishes the rebuke.
steps.raayaObject: That ישראל is one of הקב"ה's four special acquisitions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Four פסוקים using the root קנה: משלי ח, בראשית יד, תהלים עח, שמות טו.

steps.title: Pray for ישראל before praying for yourself
steps.stepSummary: הושע realizes he sinned and begins to pray for himself. הקב"ה tells him to first pray for ישראל, because three decrees were made against them because of his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once הושע knew that he had sinned, he stood up to ask for mercy for himself. הקב"ה said to him: Before you ask mercy for yourself, ask mercy for ישראל, because I made three decrees against them because of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns. הושע admits his mistake, and הקב"ה sends him to fix the damage he caused to ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three decrees are the three children's names from step 6: יזרעאל, לא רוחמה and לא עמי. Those punishments came about because הושע spoke against ישראל, so his real תשובה is to pray for them.

keyTerms.meaning: because of you, on your account

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that someone who spoke badly of ישראל fixes it by praying for them, not only for himself.

phrases.english: Once he knew that he had sinned,
he stood to request mercy for himself.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁאַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל עַצְמְךָ —
phrases.english: Before you request mercy for yourself,
request mercy for Israel,
for I have decreed three decrees against them on your account.
phrases.notes: These are the three names: יזרעאל, לא רוחמה, לא עמי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁחָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows הושע's reaction to the rebuke in steps 9 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הושע's correction is to pray for ישראל, because the three decrees came because of him.

steps.title: The decree is cancelled and the punishments become blessings
steps.stepSummary: הושע prays and the decree is cancelled. The פסוקים in הושע then turn the three punishing names (יזרעאל, לא רוחמה, לא עמי) into blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stood, asked for mercy, and cancelled the decree, and He began to bless them, as it says: "The number of בני ישראל will be like the sand of the sea... and in the place where it was said to them 'You are not My people,' it will be said to them 'Children of the living God.' And the children of יהודה and ישראל will be gathered together... And I will sow her for Me in the land, and I will have mercy on לא רוחמה, and I will say to לא עמי, 'You are My people.'"
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends happily: הושע's prayer works, and the גמרא brings פסוקים showing each bad name flipped into a good one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לא עמי" becomes "עמי אתה" and "בני אל חי." "לא רוחמה" becomes "ורחמתי." "יזרעאל" becomes "וזרעתיה," meaning I will plant her. All three decrees from step 11 are reversed into blessings.

keyTerms.meaning: like the sand of the sea (too many to count)
and I will sow/plant her (a play on the name יזרעאל)

steps.whatToRemember: הקב"ה never trades away ישראל. הושע learned this through his own family, prayed for ישראל, and the three punishing names became three blessings.

phrases.english: He stood and requested mercy, and nullified the decree,
and He began to bless them, as it is stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהָיָה מִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּחוֹל הַיָּם וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: "And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, etc.,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם
phrases.english: and in the place where it was said to them: You are not My people,
it shall be said to them: Children of the living God.

phrases.aramaic: וְנִקְבְּצוּ בְּנֵי יְהוּדָה וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יַחְדָּו וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, etc." (Hosea 2:1-2)
"And I will sow her for Me in the land,
phrases.notes: This reverses the name יזרעאל.

phrases.english: and I will have mercy on her that had not received mercy,
phrases.notes: This reverses the name לא רוחמה.

phrases.english: and I will say to Not-My-People: You are My people" (Hosea 2:25).
phrases.notes: This reverses the name לא עמי.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד וּבִקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים וּבִטֵּל גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out הקב"ה's instruction from step 11 and shows the result.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הושע's prayer for ישראל cancelled the decrees, and the three names of punishment from step 6 were turned into blessings.

steps.title: Authority buries those who hold it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that power and authority shorten a person's life. His evidence is that every נביא outlived four kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Woe to authority, because it buries the people who hold it. There is no נביא who did not outlive four kings in his lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a new statement: holding power shortens a person's life. He supports it by pointing out that every נביא outlived four kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of four kings at the start of ספר הושע leads into a new idea. Each נביא lived through four kings, so those kings must have died young. רבי יוחנן blames this on the burden of רבנות, which wears down the person who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: its owners, the people who hold it

steps.confusionAlert: קִיפֵּחַ does not mean the נביא harmed or killed the kings. It means he outlived them. The kings died while the נביא was still alive.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Woe to authority
which buries its holders.
For you do not have any prophet at all
who did not outlive four kings in his days,
phrases.notes: The kings died young because of the burden of ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אוֹי לָהּ לָרַבָּנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching. It is triggered by the list of kings in the opening פסוק of הושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Authority shortens the lives of those who hold it. The proof is that each נביא outlived four kings.

steps.title: Proof from the opening פסוק of ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק shows that ישעיהו prophesied during the reigns of four kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'The vision of ישעיהו son of אמוץ, which he saw about יהודה and ירושלים, in the days of עוזיה, יותם, אחז, and יחזקיהו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove רבי יוחנן's claim. ישעיהו lived through four kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted words end with 'וגו׳'. The proof is really in the rest of the פסוק, which names four kings of יהודה. This matches הושע 1:1, which lists the same four kings.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)

steps.confusionAlert: The four kings are not in the words the גמרא quotes. They come in the part of the פסוק hidden behind 'וגו׳'.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz'

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר חָזָה עַל יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: 'which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, etc.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues: in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That a נביא outlived four kings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 1:1, which lists four kings of יהודה in ישעיהו's lifetime.

steps.title: Why ירבעם was listed with the kings of יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says ירבעם בן יואש earned his place next to the righteous kings of יהודה because he refused to accept לשון הרע about עמוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why did ירבעם son of יואש, king of ישראל, deserve to be counted with the kings of יהודה? Because he did not accept לשון הרע about עמוס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks why a king of ישראל who was not righteous is listed next to the kings of יהודה. He answers that it was a reward for refusing to believe לשון הרע about עמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הושע 1:1 names four kings of יהודה and then one king of ישראל, ירבעם. Being named alongside those kings is treated as an honor. רבי יוחנן explains that ירבעם earned it through one good act.

keyTerms.meaning: slander, negative talk about another person

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much weight חז״ל give to refusing to accept לשון הרע. Even an imperfect king was honored for it in a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For what reason did he merit,
Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel,
to be counted with the kings of Judah?
Because he did not accept
slander about Amos.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה זָכָה יָרׇבְעָם בֶּן יוֹאָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי יוחנן, also based on the opening פסוק of הושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם was counted with the kings of יהודה because he refused to accept לשון הרע about עמוס.

steps.title: Where do we see ירבעם was counted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that ירבעם was listed together with the kings of יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that he was counted with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking for proof of the first part of רבי יוחנן's statement: that ירבעם was counted with the kings of יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's statement makes two claims. The גמרא will prove each one separately. This question targets the first claim.

phrases.english: From where do we know that he was counted?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן דְּאִימְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the first claim in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that ירבעם is listed with the kings of יהודה.

steps.title: The opening פסוק of הושע lists ירבעם
steps.stepSummary: הושע 1:1 names four kings of יהודה and then ירבעם בן יואש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'The word of ה׳ that came to הושע son of בארי, in the days of עוזיה, יותם, אחז, and יחזקיה, kings of יהודה, and in the days of ירבעם son of יואש, king of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the פסוק. It shows ירבעם named right after the four kings of יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names four kings of יהודה and then, in the same breath, ירבעם בן יואש, king of ישראל. ירבעם was not a righteous king, so being listed in one פסוק with these kings of יהודה is treated as an honor. That honor is what רבי יוחנן was explaining.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'The word of the Lord that came'
'to Hosea son of Beeri'

phrases.aramaic: בִּימֵי עֻזִּיָּה יוֹתָם אָחָז יְחִזְקִיָּה מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: 'in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah'

phrases.aramaic: וּבִימֵי יָרׇבְעָם בֶּן יוֹאָשׁ מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: 'and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״דְּבַר ה׳ אֲשֶׁר הָיָה אֶל הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן בְּאֵרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הושע 1:1 names ירבעם right after the four kings of יהודה.

steps.title: Where do we see he rejected לשון הרע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that ירבעם refused to accept לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he did not accept לשון הרע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking for proof of the second part of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first claim, that ירבעם was counted with the kings of יהודה, has been proven. Now the גמרא needs a source for the reason רבי יוחנן gave: that ירבעם refused the לשון הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he did not accept slander?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּלֹא קִיבֵּל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the second claim in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ירבעם rejected לשון הרע about עמוס.

steps.title: אמציה reports עמוס to the king
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים in עמוס describe אמציה telling ירבעם that עמוס was plotting against him and had said ירבעם would die by the sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'אמציה, the כהן of בית אל, sent to ירבעם king of ישראל, saying: עמוס has plotted against you.' And it is written: 'For thus said עמוס: ירבעם will die by the sword.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוקים in which אמציה reports to the king about עמוס. This is the לשון הרע that ירבעם was offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמציה accuses עמוס of rebellion and quotes him predicting the king's violent death. The פסוקים never say that ירבעם punished עמוס. The גמרא will explain this silence in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the city of one of ירבעם בן נבט's idol-worship centers

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Amaziah sent'
'the priest of Beth-El'
'to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying:'
'He has conspired against you, etc.'
phrases.notes: The full פסוק says it is עמוס who conspired.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'For thus said Amos:'
'Jeroboam will die by the sword, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּשְׁלַח אֲמַצְיָה כֹּהֵן בֵּית אֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 18 by showing the לשון הרע that was brought to ירבעם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים record that אמציה brought slander about עמוס to the king.

steps.title: ירבעם refuses to believe or punish עמוס
steps.stepSummary: ירבעם answered that עמוס, a צדיק, could not have said this. Even if he did, ה׳'s שכינה told him to say it, so ירבעם would not punish him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירבעם said: Heaven forbid that this צדיק said such a thing. And if he did say it, what should I do to him? The שכינה told it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by describing ירבעם's response. He refused to believe the report, and he would not punish עמוס even if it were true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירבעם gives two answers. First, he does not believe the report at all. Second, even if it is true, a נביא only passes on what the שכינה tells him, so he deserves no punishment. This is the refusal to accept לשון הרע that earned ירבעם his place in הושע 1:1.

keyTerms.meaning: the Divine Presence, ה׳ speaking to the נביא

steps.whatToRemember: ירבעם בן יואש is listed with the kings of יהודה in הושע 1:1 as a reward. He would not believe לשון הרע about עמוס, and even if it were true, he said the נביא was only passing on ה׳'s message.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two levels of rejecting לשון הרע: refusing to believe the report, and judging the person favorably even if the report is true.

phrases.english: He (Jeroboam) said: Heaven forbid
that this righteous man said such a thing,
and if he did say it, what shall I do to him?
The Divine Presence told it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אָמַר אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to step 18 by giving ירבעם's reaction to the slander.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ירבעם rejected the לשון הרע about עמוס, which proves רבי יוחנן's reason for his being counted with the kings of יהודה.

steps.title: Even in anger, God remembers compassion
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that even when הקדוש ברוך הוא is angry, He still remembers רחמים. His source is a פסוק in הושע that mentions compassion even while announcing punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Even at the time of the anger of הקדוש ברוך הוא, He remembers compassion, as it says: 'For I will no more have compassion upon the house of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר makes a new statement about how הקדוש ברוך הוא acts when He is angry, and he brings a פסוק from הושע as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is a harsh line of punishment: 'I will no longer have mercy.' Yet in the middle of that harsh line, the word ארחם (compassion) still appears. רבי אלעזר learns from this that רחמים is never fully forgotten, even in a moment of דין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)
As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק sounds like it says the opposite: 'I will NOT have mercy.' רבי אלעזר is not ignoring the word לא. His point is that God still chose to mention compassion even while holding it back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Even at the time of His anger
of the Holy One, Blessed be He
He remembers compassion.
As it is said: 'For I will no more'
phrases.notes: הושע 1:6

phrases.english: have compassion upon the house of Israel.'
phrases.notes: The word ארחם appears even in a line of punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת כַּעְסוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of ירבעם and הושע's prophecy ends, this step opens a new אגדה teaching based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even in anger, הקדוש ברוך הוא remembers רחמים, as shown by the word ארחם in a פסוק of punishment.

steps.title: A second source for compassion in anger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא brings a different source for the same idea. He uses the next words of the פסוק: 'that I should bear them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא said it is learned from here: 'That I should bear them.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא agrees with רבי אלעזר's idea but points to a different phrase as the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא points to the end of the פסוק, 'כי נשא אשא להם.' He reads it as a promise that God will one day carry and forgive ישראל's sins. So even while the punishment is being announced, a promise of forgiveness is built right into it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina
said: from here:
'That I should bear them.'
phrases.notes: End of הושע 1:6, read as a promise of future forgiveness.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative פסוק proof for the idea taught in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that God remembers רחמים even in anger.

steps.title: Exile happened so that converts would join Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא sent ישראל into גלות among the nations only so that גרים would join them. His proof is the פסוק 'And I will sow her to Me in the land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: הקדוש ברוך הוא exiled ישראל among the nations only so that converts would be added to them, as it says: 'And I will sow her to Me in the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second teaching. He explains the purpose behind גלות and supports it with a פסוק that compares ישראל to seeds being planted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the picture of planting: God 'sows' ישראל in the land. Sowing scatters seeds around, and that is like גלות scattering ישראל among the nations. The goal of sowing is growth, so the goal of גלות is growth too, meaning more people joining ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will sow her (plant her like seed)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, did not exile
Israel among the nations
except so that converts would be added to them,
as it is said: 'And I will sow her to Me in the land.'
phrases.notes: הושע 2:25

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִגְלָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבֵין הָאוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same רבי אלעזר, still based on פסוקים in הושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The purpose of גלות is that גרים will join ישראל.

steps.title: Planting a little to harvest a lot
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains why 'sowing' shows that גלות is meant to add גרים. Nobody plants a סאה of seed unless he hopes to harvest many כורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a person sow a סאה of seed for any reason other than to bring in several כורין at harvest?
steps.whatsHappening: This line explains the comparison in the פסוק and shows why 'sowing' proves רבי אלעזר's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סאה is a small measure and a כור is a much bigger one (30 סאה). A farmer gives up a little seed only because he expects a big harvest. In the same way, scattering ישראל in גלות is meant to bring back many more people, the גרים who join them.

keyTerms.meaning: Does... at all? (introduces a rhetorical question)
Kors, large measures of grain (one כור equals 30 סאה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a positive, purposeful view of גלות: it is not only a punishment but also a way of growing the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Does a person sow a se'a
for anything other than to bring in several kor?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם אָדָם זוֹרֵעַ סְאָה אֶלָּא לְהַכְנִיס כַּמָּה כּוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 23 supports רבי אלעזר's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That גלות exists in order to add גרים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The farming logic: a small amount of seed is sown to harvest a much larger yield.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source for converts joining Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a different phrase from the same פסוק: 'And I will have compassion upon her that had not received compassion.' He reads it as non-Jews who will become part of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said it is learned from here: 'And I will have compassion upon her that had not received compassion.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן supports the same idea, that גרים join ישראל, but he points to a different part of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'לא רחמה,' the one who had not received compassion, refers to people who were not part of God's nation. The פסוק continues 'and I will say to those who were not My people: you are My people.' So people from outside will come in and become part of ישראל, which means גרים.

keyTerms.meaning: She who was not shown compassion

steps.whatToRemember: There are two teachings from הושע in this section. First, God remembers רחמים even in anger (רבי אלעזר, plus a second source from רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא). Second, גלות happened so that גרים would join ישראל (רבי אלעזר using 'וזרעתיה,' and רבי יוחנן using 'ורחמתי את לא רחמה').

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: from here:
'And I will have compassion upon her that had not received compassion.'
phrases.notes: הושע 2:25

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative פסוק proof for רבי אלעזר's teaching in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That גרים will join ישראל through גלות.

steps.title: Why are the slander verse and the cursing generation verse placed together?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, points out that a פסוק forbidding slandering a servant to his master is followed right away by a פסוק about a generation that curses its father. He asks whether that really means you should not slander people who curse their parents. That reading seems absurd.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: What is the meaning of what is written, 'Do not slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you and you be found guilty,' and right after it is written, 'There is a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother'? Is it because they curse their father and do not bless their mother that you should not slander them?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens here. The גמרא points out a puzzling placement of two פסוקים in משלי and asks a question that sounds absurd. This sets up an explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the two פסוקים side by side seems to suggest that even wicked people, those who curse their parents, are protected from slander. That cannot be the point, so the question shows that a deeper reading is needed. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?
Do not slander (do not speak against)
And you will be found guilty

steps.confusionAlert: The question at the end ('Is it because they curse their father... that you should not slander?') is not a ruling. It is the גמרא showing that the simple reading makes no sense, to prepare for the real explanation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'Do not slander a servant to his master'
phrases.notes: משלי 30:10

phrases.english: 'lest he curse you and you be found guilty,'
and it is written: 'A generation that curses its father'
phrases.notes: משלי 30:11

phrases.english: 'and does not bless its mother,'
Because they curse their father
and do not bless their mother,
you should not slander them?!
phrases.notes: This is asked in surprise, because reading the פסוק that way seems absurd.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new אגדה teaching about not slandering ישראל to הקדוש ברוך הוא. Step 28 ties it back to the earlier story of הושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of the side-by-side placement of משלי 30:10 and 30:11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing the two פסוקים together would imply that people who curse their parents are protected from slander, which is unreasonable. So the placement needs a different explanation.

steps.title: Even a wicked generation must not be slandered
steps.stepSummary: The juxtaposition does not mean that people who curse their parents are protected because of their sin. It means that even when a generation is that wicked, you still may not slander them to their Master.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the point is this: even about a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother, do not slander a servant to his master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the absurd reading from the last step. The two פסוקים are placed together to teach that even a very wicked generation must not be slandered to הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that the second פסוק names who may not be slandered. The answer flips it: the second פסוק describes how bad the servants might be, and the prohibition still applies. The word אלא signals that the first reading is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the previous reading and offers the correct one
A servant to his master (here: ישראל to הקדוש ברוך הוא)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is not saying that cursing parents earns you protection from slander. It says the opposite: no matter how bad they are, you still may not speak against them.

phrases.english: Rather, even a generation
that curses its father
and does not bless its mother —
do not slander a servant to his master.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֲפִילּוּ דּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the absurd reading raised in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the juxtaposition as 'even' (אפילו) rather than as a limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second פסוק defines the people who may not be slandered
steps.terutzMaskana: The second פסוק shows that the ban applies even to a very wicked generation

steps.title: The source for this lesson is הושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn this, and answers: from הושע, who was rebuked for speaking against ישראל even though they were sinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From הושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the real-life example behind the lesson. When הושע spoke badly about sinful ישראל, הקדוש ברוך הוא was angry with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This points back to the story told earlier on the דף. הושע suggested that ישראל be exchanged for another nation, and he was rebuked even though that generation really was sinful. That story is the proof that slandering even wicked servants is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

steps.whatToRemember: Even when ישראל sin, speaking against them before הקדוש ברוך הוא is wrong. The proof is the story of הושע.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From Hosea.
phrases.notes: He means the story about הושע told earlier on this דף.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the lesson established in step 27
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one may not slander even a wicked generation
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of הושע earlier on the דף

steps.title: Scattering Israel was a kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא reads 'צדקת פרזונו' as teaching that הקדוש ברוך הוא did ישראל a kindness by scattering them among the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: What does the פסוק 'the righteousness of His rulers (פרזונו) in Israel' mean? הקדוש ברוך הוא did a kindness for ישראל by scattering them among the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the theme of גלות with a new teaching. Being spread out among many nations is described as a kindness, not only a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא reads פרזונו as related to פיזור, scattering. If all of ישראל lived in one place, an enemy could destroy them all at once. Being scattered protects the nation as a whole.

keyTerms.meaning: The righteousness of His 'rulers'; read here as 'His scattering'

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"The righteous acts of His rulers in Israel" (Judges 5:11)?
phrases.notes: פרזונו is read as related to scattering

phrases.aramaic: צְדָקָה עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, performed a kindness for Israel
in that He scattered them among the nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of גלות from steps 23-25 with a new reason why it benefits ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scattering ישראל among the nations is a kindness, because it prevents their total destruction

steps.title: A heretic boasts that Rome is kinder than Israel
steps.stepSummary: A מין tells רבי חנינא that the Romans are better than the Jews. יואב spent six months wiping out Edom's males, while Rome has ruled the Jews for years and done nothing to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what a certain heretic said to רבי חנינא: We are better than you. About you it is written, 'For six months he remained there' until every male was killed. But you have been with us for many years, and we have not done anything to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that illustrates רבי אושעיא's idea. It begins with the מין's challenge, which sets up the answer to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מין claims that Rome's restraint shows moral superiority. He contrasts it with יואב's campaign against Edom in מלכים. The answer, coming next, will show that Rome's 'restraint' is really the protection of being scattered.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what (connects a story to the teaching above)

phrases.english: And this is what was said
by a certain heretic to Rabbi Ḥanina:
We are superior to you,
for it is written about you:
"For six months he remained there, etc." (I Kings 11:16),
phrases.notes: יואב stayed until he killed every male in Edom

phrases.aramaic: וְאִלּוּ אֲנַן אִיתִינְכוּ גַּבַּן כַּמָּה שְׁנֵי
phrases.english: whereas you have been with us for many years
and we are not doing anything to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that will illustrate רבי אושעיא's teaching
steps.kashyaTarget: The moral standing of ישראל compared with Rome
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rome has not destroyed the Jews despite years of rule, while יואב destroyed Edom in six months, so Rome is supposedly more righteous

steps.title: רבי חנינא lets a student answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא asks the מין to allow one student to respond to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: With your permission, let one student deal with you.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי חנינא does not answer himself. He hands the reply to a student, and the next step gives the actual answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is argued yet. The line only introduces the person who will answer, רבי אושעיא, whose teaching opened this section.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish / with your consent

phrases.english: He said to him:
With your consent, let one student deal with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְצוֹנְךָ יִטָּפֵל לָךְ תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transition from the challenge to the answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No content yet; a student will answer

steps.title: Rome simply cannot destroy a scattered people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא answers that Rome is not kind; it just does not know how to destroy the Jews. Not all Jews are in its empire, and killing only its own Jews would make it a 'severed kingdom.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא took up the matter and said to him: It is because you do not know how to do it. To destroy all of them? They are not all with you. To destroy those who are with you? You would be called a cut-off kingdom.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers the מין's boast. Rome's 'restraint' comes from not being able to wipe out ישראל, not from goodness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly רבי אושעיא's teaching from step 29 in action. Because ישראל are scattered, no single empire can destroy them all. Killing only the Jews inside your borders would shame the empire as having cut off part of itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya took up the matter with him,
and said to him:
It is because you do not know how to do it.
Should you destroy all of them? —
They are not all with you.
Should you destroy those who are with you?
You would be called a severed kingdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְפַּל לֵיהּ רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מין's boast from step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the evidence: inaction comes from inability, not virtue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rome leaves the Jews alone because it is more righteous
steps.terutzMaskana: Rome cannot destroy a scattered people, which proves the kindness of פיזור

steps.title: The heretic admits this is Rome's constant problem
steps.stepSummary: The מין swears by a Roman god and admits that Rome struggles with this problem day and night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By the Gappa of the Romans! With this we lie down and with this we rise up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the מין admitting that רבי אושעיא is right. Rome is always thinking about how to destroy the Jews but cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His admission confirms רבי אושעיא's point. Scattering is what keeps ישראל alive, so it really is a צדקה from הקדוש ברוך הוא.

keyTerms.meaning: By Gappa (a Roman idol): an oath

steps.whatToRemember: Scattering ישראל among the nations is a kindness. No single empire can ever destroy all of them.

phrases.english: He said to him:
By Gappa, god of the Romans!
phrases.notes: He swears by it to show he agrees.

phrases.english: With this problem we lie down
and with this problem we rise up.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּפָּא דְרוֹמָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The מין concedes רבי אושעיא's answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מין's admission confirms that פיזור protects ישראל from total destruction

steps.title: Babylon was chosen because Rome's decrees were too harsh
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא knew ישראל could not survive Roman decrees, so He exiled them to בבל instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: What does the פסוק 'God understands its way, and He knows its place' mean? הקדוש ברוך הוא knows that ישראל cannot withstand the decrees of the Romans, so He exiled them to בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question: why was the exile to בבל specifically? רבי חייא gives the first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'place' in the פסוק is the place of exile, which הקדוש ברוך הוא chose carefully. Babylon was gentler than Rome, so ישראל could survive there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"God understands its way
and He knows its place" (Job 28:23)?

phrases.aramaic: יוֹדֵעַ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, knows that Israel
are unable to withstand
the decrees of the Romans.
Therefore He exiled them to Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of God's kindness in גלות, now about the choice of בבל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל were exiled to בבל because they could not survive Roman decrees

steps.title: Babylon is deep like the netherworld
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says בבל was chosen because it is low and deep like שאול. This connects to the פסוק 'From the hand of שאול I will ransom them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: הקדוש ברוך הוא exiled ישראל to בבל only because it is deep like שאול, as it says: 'From the power of the netherworld I will ransom them; from death I will redeem them.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second reason is given for why the exile was to בבל. Its low, deep land matches the פסוק promising redemption from שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Babylon is a land of low plains and valleys, so it is called 'deep like שאול.' The פסוק in הושע promises redemption from שאול. Sending ישראל there sets them up for that promised redemption.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִגְלָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבָבֶל
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, exiled Israel to Babylonia
only because it is as deep as the netherworld,
as it is stated:
"From the power of the netherworld I will ransom them,
from death I will redeem them" (Hosea 13:14).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִגְלָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason for choosing בבל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל was chosen because it is 'deep like שאול,' linking it to the promised redemption from שאול

steps.title: Babylon's language is close to the תורה's
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says בבל was chosen because its language, ארמית, is close to the language of the תורה, so the people could keep learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Because their language is close to the language of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A third reason is given for exile to בבל. Its language, ארמית, is close to לשון הקודש, which helps ישראל keep learning תורה in exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason focuses on spiritual survival rather than physical safety. A familiar language made Torah study possible even in גלות.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three reasons for exile to בבל: Rome's decrees were too harsh (רבי חייא), Babylon is 'deep like שאול' (רבי אלעזר), and its language is close to the תורה's (רבי חנינא). More reasons follow: רבי יוחנן in step 37 and עולא in step 40.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Because their language is close
to the language of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקָּרוֹב לְשׁוֹנָם לִלְשׁוֹן תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third reason for choosing בבל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל was chosen because ארמית is close to the תורה's language

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: God sent them back to their mother's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says בבל was chosen because it is the 'mother's house' of ישראל, the place their אבות came from. He compares it to a husband who is angry at his wife and sends her back to her mother's home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is because He sent them to their mother's house. This is like a man who was angry at his wife. Where does he send her? To her mother's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives another reason why the exile was to בבל: it was where the Jewish people's family originally came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם אבינו and the family of the אבות came from the area of בבל (ארם נהרים). So exile to בבל was not throwing ישראל away. It was like an angry husband sending his wife to her mother, which shows anger but leaves room to make up later.

keyTerms.meaning: their mother's house, meaning their place of origin

steps.confusionAlert: The 'mother's house' is not a real house. It means בבל, the homeland of the אבות before they came to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because He sent them to their mother's house.
phrases.notes: Babylonia, where the forefathers came from.

phrases.english: A parable: a man who was angry at his wife,
where does he send her? To her mother's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשִּׁיגְּרָן לְבֵית אִמָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reason for exile to בבל, alongside רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל was chosen because it is the place of origin of the אבות, the 'mother's house' of ישראל.

steps.title: רבי אלכסנדרי: three things returned to their origin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects רבי יוחנן's idea to the teaching of רבי אלכסנדרי. He says three things went back to where they came from: ישראל, the money of מצרים, and the writing on the לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this matches what רבי אלכסנדרי said: Three things returned to their place of origin. They are: ישראל, the money of מצרים, and the writing on the לוחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן from a teaching of רבי אלכסנדרי. It first lists the three things, and the next step proves each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלכסנדרי's list includes ישראל returning to their origin, which is exactly רבי יוחנן's point about the 'mother's house.' The word והיינו means 'this is the same idea,' so this step backs up רבי יוחנן rather than adding a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is the same as
to their place of planting, meaning their origin

phrases.english: And this is the teaching of Rabbi Alexandri, who said:
Three returned to their place of origin,
and these are they: the Jewish people,
the money of Egypt, and the writing on the Tablets.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's 'mother's house' idea with a parallel teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that ישראל were sent back to their origin
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלכסנדרי's list of three things that returned to their origin

steps.title: Proving each of the three returns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each item. ישראל went back to בבל, as just said. The money of מצרים went back when שישק king of מצרים took Jerusalem's treasures. The letters of the לוחות flew back up to heaven when the לוחות were broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישראל: what we just said. The money of מצרים, as it is written: 'In the fifth year of King רחבעם, שישק king of מצרים came up against ירושלים...' The writing of the לוחות, as it is written: 'And I broke them before your eyes.' A ברייתא taught: The לוחות broke, and the letters flew away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a source for each of the three things on רבי אלכסנדרי's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישראל took Egypt's money at יציאת מצרים, and later שישק carried the Temple and royal treasures back to מצרים. When משה broke the לוחות, the stone broke but the holy letters 'flew away,' returning to heaven where they came from. This finishes the support for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Exile to בבל was a 'return home' to the place of the אבות, just as Egypt's money and the letters of the לוחות went back to where they came from.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the פסוק's opening words are quoted. The proof is in the rest of the פסוק, which says שישק took the treasures of the בית המקדש and the king's house.

phrases.english: The Jewish people: that which we just said.
The money of Egypt, as it is written:
"And it was in the fifth year of King Rehoboam

phrases.aramaic: עָלָה שִׁישַׁק מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, etc."
phrases.notes: He took the treasures back to Egypt.

phrases.english: The writing on the Tablets, as it is written:
"And I broke them before your eyes,"
It was taught: The Tablets were broken and the letters flew away.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִשְׂרָאֵל — הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for each item in רבי אלכסנדרי's list.
steps.raayaObject: Each of the three returns in רבי אלכסנדרי's list

steps.title: עולא begins a new reason: so they could eat
steps.stepSummary: עולא starts to give his own reason for exile to בבל: 'so that they could eat...' The rest of his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: In order that they could eat...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. עולא begins another reason for exile to בבל, but the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new reason, separate from רבי יוחנן's 'mother's house.' עולא's reason is about food, meaning a physical benefit for ישראל in exile. His full point is completed on the next amud.

phrases.english: Ulla said: In order that they eat...
phrases.notes: Statement continues on the next amud.
